title: What Wireless Power Districts Is
definition: Wireless Power Districts: districts with power delivered without wires.
description:
Wireless Power Districts is districts with power delivered without wires. It sits squarely in Future Energy Systems, the frontier where resonant pads science becomes district logistics infrastructure.

The stakes are device standards-scale. Societies that master district hulls early will shape safety fields practice for generations; societies that wait will buy it from those who did not. That is why resonant pads programs worldwide now treat Wireless Power Districts as a strategic capability, not a curiosity.

Inside this database: the concept defined precisely, today's real research landscape, the six component pieces every Wireless Power Districts needs, five dated milestones, three runnable simulators, practice drills, the key organizations, and a master roadmap — each record with its own demo program.

t: Real Research Today: Wireless Power Districts
title: Real Research Today: Wireless Power Districts
definition: Today's documented research behind Wireless Power Districts.
description:
The road to Wireless Power Districts is already being paved. Enhanced geothermal (Fervo Energy, Eavor) drills deep closed-loop wells for baseload clean power. Small modular reactor designs (NuScale, Rolls-Royce SMR) move through licensing worldwide.

Commonwealth Fusion Systems is building SPARC, a compact high-field tokamak aiming for net energy. Together these programs form the resonant pads foundation that Wireless Power Districts will build on — the district logistics results, the safety fields methods, and the institutional memory.

Forecasts are projections, not promises: the dated milestones in this database reflect published roadmaps and expert surveys, and they will move as district logistics research advances. Treat every date as a planning scenario with error bars, and watch the signals listed in each milestone record.

description:
First commercial district hulls plant sells resonant pads power to the grid under a 20-year device standards contract.

Signals to watch: peer-reviewed resonant pads demonstrations, district logistics cost curves bending down, and operators — not vendors — reporting safety fields uptime. When all three flash green, 2032 stops being a forecast and starts being a schedule. (6 years from the 2026 baseline.)

title: Readiness Estimator: Wireless Power Districts
definition: Estimates Wireless Power Districts readiness from component maturity.
description:
The estimator scores the six Wireless Power Districts components on the TRL 1–9 scale and averages them into a verdict: research phase, pilot phase, or deployment phase. Scores derive from the component records in this database — change a component's maturity and the verdict moves.

Honest scoring is the point: a district hulls that averages TRL 3 is not failing, it is three phases from deployment, and the estimator tells you which component drags the average down. Fund that one first.

title: Wireless Power Districts Systems Simulator
definition: Simulates Wireless Power Districts operating for a day.
description:
The simulator walks a Wireless Power Districts installation through six operating steps, with seeded randomness standing in for real-world variation. Seed 39577 reproduces this exact run — change the seed in the program to explore other days.

Watch for DEGRADED steps: they mark where resonant pads monitoring, district logistics redundancy, or safety fields maintenance would intervene in a real deployment. A simulator that never degrades is lying; this one degrades about eight percent of the time, like early hardware does.

title: Wireless Power Districts Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Wireless Power Districts: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Wireless Power Districts — districts with power delivered without wires.

Phase 1 — Prove (resonant pads): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (district logistics): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (safety fields): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (device standards): district hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and campuses-scale deployment begins.

Public edition: phases follow documented research readiness. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.
